question.text: What will the EIA report as the week-over-week change in U.S. commercial crude oil inventories (excluding SPR) for the week ending 6 November 2026?
question.resolution_criteria: This question resolves on the "Week-on-week change for United States" figure for commercial crude oil stocks (excluding the Strategic Petroleum Reserve) reported in the EIA's Weekly Petroleum Status Report for the week ending 6 November 2026, scheduled for publication at 12:00 p.m. ET (17:00 UTC) on 12 November 2026 at https://www.eia.gov/petroleum/supply/weekly/. The answer is that figure in thousand barrels, with a draw reported as a negative number: for example, the −1,892 thousand barrels reported for the week ending 23 October 2026 resolves as −1892. If EIA's release for that week is delayed, the question resolves once the figure is published. Should the WPSR page no longer display that week, the figure may be taken as the week-ending stock level for 6 November 2026 minus that for 30 October 2026 from EIA's weekly ending-stocks series (https://www.eia.gov/dnav/pet/hist/LeafHandler.ashx?n=PET&s=WCESTUS1&f=W).
question.fine_print: The resolving figure is the one published in the 12 November 2026 release; later revisions to either week's stock level do not change the resolution.

research:
I'm writing up the findings now. I pulled the EIA weekly series, the latest WPSR tables and the recent news.

## 1. Resolution source
- 2026-10-28 release (week ending 2026-10-23): commercial crude excluding SPR was 410,625 thousand bbl, down from 412,517, a change of -1,892. That is the latest published week. The SPR held 282,583 thousand bbl (-100), against 409,097 a year earlier. Refinery crude inputs were 16,526 kb/d (prior week 16,649). Commercial crude imports were 6,374 kb/d (prior 5,758). Exports were 4,854 kb/d (prior 3,442). Production was 13,992 kb/d (prior 13,269). The crude adjustment was +189 kb/d. [EIA table1.csv](https://ir.eia.gov/wpsr/table1.csv)
- The WPSR landing page didn't show the headline numbers in the text I could read. The figures are in the linked tables. [EIA WPSR](https://www.eia.gov/petroleum/supply/weekly/)

## 2. Current status
- Nothing has settled the question. The week ending 30 Oct is due 2026-11-04 and the target week (ending 6 Nov) is due 2026-11-12. Neither the API figure nor any EIA figure for either week was available as of today.

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-11-02: WTI fell about 6.5% to $97.32 and Brent fell to $106.30 on hopes of US-Iran peace talks through Qatar. The war has lasted about eight months and the Strait of Hormuz has been closed since March. [Invezz](https://invezz.com/cz/zpravodajstvi/2026/11/02/cena-ropy-dnes-wti-klesa-pod-dollar100-rostou-nadeje-na-mir-s-iranem/), [MarketScreener](https://www.marketscreener.com/news/us-stock-index-futures-jump-as-oil-falls-about-6-ce785fd9d989f520)
- 2026-11-01: OPEC+ kept December supply unchanged. [PR Newswire](https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/oil-enters-november-with-opec-holding-steady-and-five-producers-set-to-report-302926283.html)
- 2026-10-28: The EIA reported a 1.9 mb draw. One analyst said that "on measured flows it drew -7.1 mb", meaning the adjustment term offset most of the draw. The API had estimated -2.03 mb. [The Oil Report](https://www.theoilreport.pro/p/eia-inventories-084), [Rigzone](https://www.rigzone.com/news/usa_crude_oil_stocks_drop_week_on_week-30-oct-2026-184983-article/)
- October 2026: four straight weekly draws: -3.2 mb (2 Oct, when exports rose 1.2 mb/d to 4.77), -8.6 mb (9 Oct), -3.1 mb (16 Oct, partly tied to hurricane disruption) and -1.9 mb (23 Oct). Strong exports and refinery runs were cited. [Hydrocarbon Processing](https://www.hydrocarbonprocessing.com/news/2026/10/eia-us-crude-stocks-fall-amid-strong-exports-refining-activity/), [Energies Media](https://energiesmedia.com/eia-us-crude-inventories-drop-2)
- An Oilandgas360 page dated "October 25, 2026" shows +0.9 mb and 427.3 mb. Those numbers don't match the EIA data, so the page looks mislabeled. [Oilandgas360](https://www.oilandgas360.com/crude-inventories-9-25/)

## 4. Base rates
- 2026 levels in thousand bbl, from the EIA series: 22 May 441,686, then a steady decline to 404,508 on 24 Jul, then +17,423 in the week to 7 Aug. Since then: 428,910 (21 Aug), 427,320 (25 Sep), 424,134 (2 Oct), 410,625 (23 Oct). Weekly moves of 4 to 9 mb have been common this year, and the largest was +17.4 mb. [EIA series](https://www.eia.gov/dnav/pet/hist/LeafHandler.ashx?n=PET&s=WCESTUS1&f=W)
- Change for the comparable early-November week, from the same series:
  - 2021 (5 Nov): +1,002
  - 2022 (4 Nov): +3,925
  - 2023 (3 Nov): +13,869. That was the period when EIA delayed releases for a systems upgrade, so treat it with caution.
  - 2024 (8 Nov): +2,089
  - 2025 (7 Nov): +6,413

  All five years were builds. That fits the seasonal pattern of autumn refinery maintenance reducing crude runs.
- The following week was mixed: 2021 -2,101, 2022 -5,400, 2023 +3,592, 2024 +545, 2025 -3,426.
- The typical weekly spread is roughly ±4 to 5 mb (one standard deviation, my rough reading of the series above). The API and EIA figures often differ by more than 1 mb, and in the 2025 equivalent week the API showed +6.52 mb. [SunSirs](https://www.sunsirs.com/uk/detail_news-27685.html)

## 5. Other forecasts
- Kalshi has a market on the level for the week ending **30 Oct** (the prior week, not the target week). As of 2026-11-02 17:04 UTC, "Above 410 mb" was 0.54 and "Above 411 mb" was 0.48. That puts the implied median around 410.5 to 411 mb, roughly flat against 410.6 mb. "Above 406" was 0.84 and "Above 415" was 0.24.
- I found no market or analyst consensus for the week ending 6 Nov. I also found no analyst poll yet for the week ending 30 Oct.

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- 2026-11-03 (Tue): API estimate for the week ending 30 Oct.
- 2026-11-04 (Wed, 10:30 ET): EIA WPSR for the week ending 30 Oct, which sets the starting level for this question.
- 2026-11-10 (Tue): API estimate for the week ending 6 Nov.
- 2026-11-12 (Thu, 12:00 ET): EIA release that resolves the question. It is delayed because of Veterans Day.
- Other things that could move the number:
  - The pace of US crude exports, which was elevated at 4.85 mb/d while the Hormuz crisis keeps overseas demand for US barrels high.
  - Refinery maintenance and utilisation, which was around 92.8%.
  - Swings in the crude adjustment term.
  - SPR activity. The SPR is very depleted at 282.6 mb and its weekly changes are small.
  - Any US-Iran ceasefire news that shifts the price structure and export economics.

Sources: [EIA series](https://www.eia.gov/dnav/pet/hist/LeafHandler.ashx?n=PET&s=WCESTUS1&f=W), [EIA table1](https://ir.eia.gov/wpsr/table1.csv), [EIA WPSR](https://www.eia.gov/petroleum/supply/weekly/), [Hydrocarbon Processing](https://www.hydrocarbonprocessing.com/news/2026/10/eia-us-crude-stocks-fall-amid-strong-exports-refining-activity/), [Rigzone](https://www.rigzone.com/news/usa_crude_oil_stocks_drop_week_on_week-30-oct-2026-184983-article/), [The Oil Report](https://www.theoilreport.pro/p/eia-inventories-084), [Energies Media](https://energiesmedia.com/eia-us-crude-inventories-drop-2), [Oilandgas360](https://www.oilandgas360.com/crude-inventories-9-25/), [SunSirs](https://www.sunsirs.com/uk/detail_news-27685.html), [Invezz](https://invezz.com/cz/zpravodajstvi/2026/11/02/cena-ropy-dnes-wti-klesa-pod-dollar100-rostou-nadeje-na-mir-s-iranem/), [MarketScreener](https://www.marketscreener.com/news/us-stock-index-futures-jump-as-oil-falls-about-6-ce785fd9d989f520), [PR Newswire](https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/oil-enters-november-with-opec-holding-steady-and-five-producers-set-to-report-302926283.html)

forecasts.reasoning:
(a) **Time left:** about 10 days. The EIA release is on 12 November 2026 at 17:00 UTC. The 30 October week's data comes out on 4 November, and the API estimate for the target week comes out on 10 November.

(b) **Latest known value:** for the week ending 23 October 2026, commercial crude stocks were 410,625 thousand bbl, a weekly change of -1,892.

(c) **If nothing changed:** a change of 0.

(d) **If the current trend continued:** there have been four straight draws, averaging about -4.2 mb per week over October. If that continued, the 6 November week would show roughly -2,000 to -4,000. That is driven by strong exports (about 4.85 mb/d) while the Strait of Hormuz is closed.

(e) **Historical variation:** weekly changes have a standard deviation of roughly 4 to 5 mb. This year, swings of 4 to 9 mb have been common, with one outlier of +17.4 mb. The comparable early-November week was a build in each of the last five years (+1.0, +3.9, +13.9, +2.1, +6.4 mb), consistent with refinery maintenance.

(f) **Expert and market expectations:**
- Kalshi's market for the prior week (ending 30 October) implies a median of about 410.5 to 411 mb, which is roughly flat on the week.
- There is no market or analyst consensus yet for the target week.
- My weighting: the seasonal tendency toward builds and the market's flat expectation offset the recent draw trend. That puts my median near zero, slightly positive.

(g) **Unexpected scenarios:**
- **Low:** exports surge above 6 mb/d, refineries return from maintenance at high runs, imports collapse and the adjustment term swings negative. That could produce a draw of 10 mb or more.
- **High:** peace-talk headlines flip the price structure, export cargoes are deferred, imports bunch up and a refinery outage cuts runs. That could produce a build of 10 to 13 mb or more.
